source.author: Raysonho @ Open Grid Scheduler / Grid Engine

analysis.summary: Black wired Lenovo mouse viewed from above-rear on white background, showing curved top shell, integrated click buttons, red scroll wheel, and attached cable extending out of frame.

components.name: Top housing / palm shell
components.function: Encloses internal electronics and provides ergonomic hand support
components.evidence: Matte black domed shell with Lenovo logo on rear and visible side contour and reflections on top surface

components.name: Integrated left/right click buttons
components.function: Transmit press inputs for primary selection actions
components.evidence: Paired seam lines flanking the scroll wheel on the forward dorsal surface of the housing

components.name: Scroll wheel
components.function: Enables vertical scrolling and middle-click input
components.evidence: Small red ridged wheel protruding in central gap between button seams at front of mouse

components.name: Wired cable
components.function: Carries power and data between mouse and host computer
components.evidence: Thin black flexible cable exiting from front center and curving across upper right of image

components.name: Optical tracking sensor assembly (underside)
components.function: Illuminates surface and detects motion to translate into cursor movement
components.evidence: Not visible in top-down view; inferred as typical hidden component for modern wired mice rather than ball-type

components.name: Internal PCB with microswitches and controller
components.function: Registers button/wheel inputs and communicates via wired protocol to computer
components.evidence: Internal structure not photographed; inferred as standard hidden electronics beneath housing and buttons

principles.name: Hinged button actuation via microswitch
principles.explanation: Pressing the flexible top shell/button area likely deflects to actuate a tactile microswitch on the internal PCB, creating an electrical click signal

principles.name: Optical motion tracking
principles.explanation: Hidden underside sensor likely illuminates the surface with LED and captures sequential images to compute displacement, sent as cursor data through the cable

principles.name: Rotary encoder scroll input
principles.explanation: Rotation of the visible wheel likely turns an internal encoder that generates scroll pulses, with a press action for middle-click

uncertainty: Underside sensor model, resolution, or connector type not visible in this single top view
Internal PCB layout, switch types, and controller specifications cannot be established from photo
Exact materials, manufacturing date, or model number not legible beyond Lenovo logo
Surface texture, weight, cable length, and bottom glide pads not shown
Whether mouse uses USB-A, USB-C, or other interface at cable end outside frame
next_steps: Photograph underside, front, and side views to document sensor opening, feet, and cable entry
Capture close-up of scroll wheel and button seams in good lighting without opening the device
If label present underneath, photograph regulatory markings for model identification
safety_notes: Do not disassemble or cut cable; internal electronics carry low voltage but sharp edges and small parts present risk
This analysis identifies visible external features only and cannot verify electrical safety or functionality
Avoid using damaged cables to prevent intermittent connection or overheating at host port
